core_obligations: Reformulate the statement (proof lines 11796-11798): the assertion means that if X is covered by opens U_i on which the restriction of F is constructible, then F itself is constructible.

Reduce to affine opens (proof lines 11798-11801): for an affine open U of X, the intersections U cap U_i form an open covering of U, and each restriction F|_{U cap U_i} is constructible because restriction of a constructible sheaf to an open is constructible.

Apply the affine criterion (proof lines 11801-11804): by the cited same-chapter result, constructibility of F|_U follows, that is, a suitable partition of U exists, and this for every affine open U of X, which gives the constructibility of F.
proof_roadmap: Rewrite locality of constructibility as the statement that constructibility on the members of an open covering implies constructibility.
For an affine open U, restrict the given covering and use that restriction to an open preserves constructibility.
Apply the same-chapter criterion for affine quasi-compact schemes to conclude for F|_U.
Since affine opens cover X, conclude for F.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that constructibility of a sheaf on X_etale can be checked Zariski locally (statement lines 11788-11793). The proof is a short reduction with one non-formal step: for an affine open U one restricts the given open covering to U cap U_i, uses that restriction of a constructible sheaf to an open is constructible, and then invokes the same-chapter criterion producing a partition of U from constructible restrictions on a finite open covering (proof lines 11796-11804). The content is the reduction to the affine criterion, which is what makes the locality statement usable. The claim is H2: one reduction plus a cited criterion.
